items.front: Who devised the three-age (Stone–Bronze–Iron) archaeological system, and when?
items.examPoint: Stone Age definition & Thomson's three-age system (1820)
items.source: APPSC GK — Ancient History: Stone Age

items.front: Who coined 'Palaeolithic' (1865), and what are its people called?
items.back: John Lubbock; people called 'Quartzite Men' after their quartzite tools.
items.examPoint: Palaeolithic naming — John Lubbock (1865), Quartzite Men, Pleistocene/Ice Age
items.source: APPSC GK — Ancient History: Stone Age

items.front: Name the three Stone Age periods with their spans.
items.back: Palaeolithic (up to 10,000 BC) → Mesolithic (9000–4000 BC) → Neolithic (4000–1000 BC).
items.source: APPSC GK — Ancient History: Stone Age

items.front: Characteristic tools of Lower / Middle / Upper Palaeolithic?
items.back: Lower: hand axes, cleavers, choppers. Middle: blades, points, borers. Upper: burins, scrapers, flint.
items.source: APPSC GK — Ancient History: Stone Age

items.front: Who discovered the Pallavaram Hand Axe (1863), the 'Father of Indian Pre-history'?
items.examPoint: Pre-history archaeologists — Cunningham (first ASI Director, 1861) & R.B. Foote (Pallavaram Hand Axe)
items.source: APPSC GK — Ancient History: Stone Age

items.front: First Director of the Archaeological Survey of India (1861)?
items.examPoint: Pre-history archaeologists — Cunningham (first ASI Director, 1861) & R.B. Foote (Pallavaram Hand Axe)
items.source: APPSC GK — Ancient History: Stone Age

items.front: Mesolithic Age: which epoch, and its signature tools?
items.back: Holocene era; microliths (~1–2 cm flint/chert) hafted into spears, harpoons and arrows.
items.source: APPSC GK — Ancient History: Stone Age

items.front: Oldest known Neolithic site in the Indian subcontinent, and its date?
items.examPoint: Neolithic Age (New Stone Age, 4000–1000 BC) — polished tools, agriculture, Mehrgarh (oldest, 7000 BC)
items.source: APPSC GK — Ancient History: Stone Age

items.front: Neolithic site famous for pit dwellings and dogs buried with humans?
items.back: Burzahom (Kashmir) — dog burials indicate belief in an afterlife.
items.examPoint: Neolithic settlements & developments (Burzahom pit dwellings & dog burials, wheel & fire, Chirand bone tools)
items.source: APPSC GK — Ancient History: Stone Age

items.front: Neolithic site in Bihar famous for bone tools and weapons?
items.examPoint: Neolithic settlements & developments (Burzahom pit dwellings & dog burials, wheel & fire, Chirand bone tools)
items.source: APPSC GK — Ancient History: Stone Age

items.front: Chalcolithic (Copper) Age: signature pottery and cultivation type?
items.back: Black and Red Ware (BRW), wheel-made; Jhum (shifting) cultivation. Span 3500–1000 BC.
items.examPoint: Chalcolithic Age (Copper Age, 3500–1000 BC) — BRW, Jhum, Ganeshwar/Jodhpura
items.source: APPSC GK — Ancient History: Stone Age

items.front: Which Chalcolithic culture had a chalcedony blade-flake industry?
items.examPoint: Chalcolithic cultures & features (Ahar-Banas, Kayatha, Malwa, Savalda, Jorwe, Prabhas-Rangpur; social inequality)
items.source: APPSC GK — Ancient History: Stone Age

items.front: Bhimbetka rock shelters (MP): significance and UNESCO listing year?
items.back: Largest prehistoric rock-art complex; inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2003.
items.examPoint: Bhimbetka & prehistoric art sites (Belan Valley, Narmada Valley; UNESCO)
items.source: APPSC GK — Ancient History: Stone Age; UNESCO WHC

items.front: Megalithic culture of South India: burial box, metal, and irrigation innovation?
items.back: Cists (stone boxes); iron artifacts; introduced tank irrigation. Described in Sangam literature.
items.examPoint: Megalithic culture of South India (cists, iron, tank irrigation, Sangam literature)
items.source: APPSC GK — Ancient History: Stone Age
